sections.h2: Which Laurel County offices touch a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices in and around London split the job. One values the property, one collects the money, and one inherits whatever stays unpaid. Calling the wrong one costs a seller time, so here is who does what.

  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA): Room 127 at 101 S. Main St. Call (606) 864-2889. The office closes at 4:30 Monday through Friday, and its website runs parcel searches by street address, owner name or parcel number.
  • Sheriff: 1380 East Hwy 192. Call 606-864-6600. Counter service ends at 4:00 on weekdays, and Saturday and Sunday are closed.
  • County Clerk: Room 203 at the same Main Street address, phone (606) 864-5158. The clerk receives delinquent bills and runs the sale of the liens.

Ask the sheriff or the PVA for the exact rate that applies to your parcel, since a countywide average will not fit every address.

sections.h2: What should an owner know about Laurel County itself?
sections.html:
The state cut Laurel County out of four older counties in December 1825, and it now covers about 434 square miles of land. London is the seat. Corbin lies mostly across the border in Whitley County. Part of the Daniel Boone National Forest and of Laurel River Lake lie inside the lines. History buffs know it for the Civil War fight at Wildcat Mountain, and visitors for the first Kentucky Fried Chicken cafe north of Corbin and the World Chicken Festival in London.

  • Population: an estimated 63,746 in July 2025, with a 2020 density of 144 residents per square mile.
  • Older residents: 19.1 percent are 65 or above, the group that can claim the homestead exemption described below.
  • Housing: 27,063 units, 23,996 households, 71.6 percent owned by their occupants.
  • Middle home value $159,500. Owners with a mortgage carry median monthly costs of $1,239, and owners without one report $382.
  • The Census Bureau counted 21 building permits for the county in 2025.
  • Retail sales reached about $1.68 billion in 2022, and the county's mean commute is 22.6 minutes, so many owners work close to home.
  • Median household income runs $57,771, and 89.0 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which points to a stable base of long-term owners.

sections.h2: What are the Laurel County payment dates and penalties?
sections.html:
The assessment date is New Year's Day, and the tax for that year is due at the sheriff's office before December 31 ends. KRS 134.015 turns the calendar into money.

  • Pay in full by November 1 and the bill drops 2 percent.
  • From November 2 through December, the number printed on the bill is what you pay.
  • In January a 5 percent penalty applies.
  • From February 1 the penalty is 10 percent.

If bills are late getting out, the state can swap in a shifted timetable with a discount month followed by a face-value month. The sheriff's page lists three routes: walk in, mail a check, or leave one in the box on the building's front. Cards work at the office only. Keep cash out of the mail and the box, and tuck in a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt.

sections.h2: How can a Laurel County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
Start by talking to the PVA or a deputy, since the local board will not hear an owner who skipped that step. The roll is posted for public viewing in May, beginning the first Monday and running thirteen days with Saturdays counted. The written appeal goes to the county clerk, and the deadline is one workday after the viewing period ends.

The board convenes about a month after viewing ends. Bring proof such as sales of similar houses, an insurance policy, what the building cost, or a description of the lot. With nothing on paper the board turns the appeal down, and skipping the hearing closes the later door to the Kentucky Claims Commission. Bills that print mid-dispute use the owner's number, and a supplemental bill follows if the board's value comes out higher.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for homestead relief in Laurel County?
sections.html:
The exemption takes $49,100 off the home's assessment for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, so a $200,000 house is taxed as if it were worth $150,900. It is open to owners 65 or older and to owners classified as totally disabled. About 19.1 percent of Laurel County residents are 65 or older, so many sellers here may already have it on file.

Apply at the PVA's Room 127 office with proof of age or disability. Disability claims are renewed every year, with exceptions for veterans with a service connected disability and for anyone already ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems. Ask the PVA how the exemption is treated after the house is sold.

sections.h2: What does a delinquent Laurel County tax bill turn into?
sections.html:
After the April 15 close of collection, the sheriff sends every open bill to the clerk, which records a lien on the land and calls the bill a certificate of delinquency. Interest of 1 percent then runs for each month or fraction of a month. The Department of Revenue's own sample starts with a $1,000 bill that becomes $1,254 at the handoff, assuming a 4 percent sheriff commission, then keeps climbing as the clerk and county attorney add their shares.

A $1,000 Kentucky bill as it ages in the clerk's office (Department of Revenue examples)
When it is settledAmount
On the day the sheriff transfers it$1,254.00
Within five business days of the transfer$1,387.79
After the county attorney's first letter$1,611.30
In May$1,627.61
After the June newspaper listing$1,659.90
By an outside buyer at the sale$1,704.21

The clerk must hold the sale at least 90 and at most 135 days after the transfer. The Laurel County Clerk's notice for the 2026 sale had outside buyers registering August 17 through August 31 with a deposit of 25 percent of their list value, and that registration window is over. KRS 134.015 keeps the tax lien alive for eleven years whoever holds title.

sections.h2: What tax steps should a Laurel County seller finish before listing?
sections.html:
• Get a statement from the sheriff showing this year's bill and any older year still open.
  • Ask the clerk's delinquent tax staff whether a certificate already exists against the parcel.
  • Check the PVA website to confirm owner name, parcel number and assessed value.
  • If the homestead exemption is on file, ask the PVA what changes at the sale.
  • Put a split of the current year's bill in the sales contract so the closing agent knows who owes what.

Sellers who want to skip repairs can request a direct offer. Any tax still owed comes out of the proceeds at the closing table.

faqs.q: Where does a Laurel County owner pay the tax bill?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's office, 1380 East Hwy 192, London. Payment is accepted at the counter with a card, by mailed check and at the drop box outside.

faqs.q: How big is the early payment discount in Laurel County?
faqs.a: Two percent, for a bill the sheriff has received in full by November 1 of the assessment year. After that the printed amount applies until the end of December.

faqs.q: Which office handles a disagreement over value?
faqs.a: The PVA, at (606) 864-2889. An owner who wants to appeal must meet with the PVA or a deputy first.

faqs.q: What is the Kentucky homestead exemption worth in 2026?
faqs.a: It lowers the assessed value by $49,100 for qualifying owners aged 65 or older or totally disabled. The PVA takes the application.

faqs.q: Does a tax lien stay with the property after a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. KRS 134.015 lets a delinquent tax lien run for eleven years regardless of who owns the land, so a buyer's title agent searches for it.
